<a id="edition-cases-radio-telegram-priority"></a>

## Request for replies and radio priority

**Sources on this page:** p128 A1, p128 A2. [Concise case study](../radio/telegram_priority.md).

<a id="edition-cases-radio-telegram-priority-request-for-replies-and-radio-priority"></a>



**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

This two-part telegram asks the Foreign Office in Berlin for replies to
three earlier messages and for brief instructions in plaintext. It then
suggests explicitly telling the radio station to send these telegrams
before others, because military telegrams apparently receive priority.
The signature is the literal `HORSTMANN`; no historical identity is assigned
from the name alone.

Both printed frames are complete: **226 and 282 slots**, under the unchanged
published `Nov4-6` key. Six observed-coordinate substitutions and seven
printed-dash fills give the readable edition. No coordinate is inserted,
removed or reordered, and no square cell is changed.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-telegram-priority-source-and-the-first-part"></a>

### Source and the first part

The primary source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher
System*, [printed p128, PDF p131](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view).
The [full page](../../experiments/radio_telegram_priority/sources/childs_p128_full.png)
is headed `5th NOVEMBER, 1918.` The shared header is:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
A) LP v NKJ (7.01 p.m., November 5th)
1130 (5) 2 TLE
```

</details>

The [first part](../../experiments/radio_telegram_priority/sources/childs_p128_A1.png)
is labeled `1 TL RICHI-226`. All 226 coordinates are valid and fix all
113 raw plaintext positions:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
AUSWAERTIGBERLINNUMMER597XANTWORTAUFTELEGRAMME569X592UND598BISHERNICHTEINGETROFFENXZURZEWEISUNGINKLARTEXTERBETENX
```

</details>

One coordinate substitution changes `ZURZE` to `KURZE`:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
AUSWAERTIGBERLINNUMMER597XANTWORTAUFTELEGRAMME569X592UND598BISHERNICHTEINGETROFFENXKURZEWEISUNGINKLARTEXTERBETENX
```

</details>

Readable German:

**Readable German:**

> Auswärtig Berlin. Nummer 597. Antwort auf Telegramme 569, 592 und 598
> bisher nicht eingetroffen. Kurze Weisung in Klartext erbeten.

The telegram says that replies to messages **569, 592 and 598** have not
yet arrived and requests brief instructions in plaintext. The message
number **597** and all three references are unchanged labels from the
published square; the edition does not infer a chronology from their order.
The source's `AUSWAERTIG` remains an abbreviation, without inserting an
encoded `AMT` into the plaintext.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-telegram-priority-second-part-proposed-radio-precedence"></a>

### Second part: proposed radio precedence

The [second part](../../experiments/radio_telegram_priority/sources/childs_p128_A2.png)
is labeled `2 TL RICHI-282`. It contains exactly 282 printed slots, including
seven dashes. Its ordinary source frame fixes 134 of 141 positions:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
ANH9IMGRSTELLTFDNKENSTATIONAUSDRUEK?IC7?NZUHEISENXTELEGRAMMEVORALLENANDERENZUGEBENXD?SCHEINBAR?ILITAER?SCHETELE?RAMME?EVORZUGTWERDNXHORSTMANN
```

</details>

Five observed-coordinate substitutions and seven dash fills give:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
ANHEIMGESTELLTFUNKENSTATIONAUSDRUEKLICHANZUWEISENXTELEGRAMMEVORALLENANDERENZUGEBENXDASCHEINBARMILITAERISCHETELEGRAMMEBEVORZUGTWERDNXHORSTMANN
```

</details>

Its meaning is: it is suggested that the wireless station be explicitly
instructed to send these telegrams before all others, because military
telegrams apparently receive preferential treatment. This is a suggestion
to the recipient, not evidence that such an instruction had already been
issued or obeyed.

The literal spellings **`AUSDRUEKLICH`** and **`WERDN`** remain in the edition.
No additional plaintext `C` or `E` is claimed. The signature `HORSTMANN`
already appears unchanged in the raw reading.

An earlier OCR extraction supplied only 281 slots. Manual source review
establishes the advertised 282-slot frame. This is an OCR transcription
correction and supplies no evidence for a historical before-transposition
coordinate loss.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-telegram-priority-verification-and-attribution"></a>

### Verification and attribution

The [inputs](../../experiments/radio_telegram_priority/inputs.json) preserve
the exact headers, manual groups, key provenance and image hashes. The
[certificate](../../experiments/radio_telegram_priority/certificates.json)
retains every raw domain, source-coordinate origin, repair, dash fill,
numerical label and full forward witness. The standard-library verifier
independently undoes the transposition and rebuilds both witnesses:

```sh
python experiments/radio_telegram_priority/verify.py --verify
```

The period key is prior work by **George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and
Arno Wacker**, [DOI 10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461](https://doi.org/10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461),
also reproduced in George Lasry's [2017-02-24 comment 4](https://scienceblogs.de/klausis-krypto-kolumne/2017/02/23/the-top-50-unsolved-encrypted-messages-46-unsolved-adfgvx-cryptograms-from-world-war-1/?all=1).
Earlier unreviewed OCR-derived candidates existed. The bounded author-paper
check found no explicit p128 A body example; that does not establish
universal first-decipherment priority. Exact re-encryption certifies the
stated arithmetic and repair prices, not unique historical wording.

<a id="edition-cases-military-transylvania-situation-report"></a>

## Surviving Transylvania situation report

**Sources on this page:** p128 B1. [Concise case study](../military/transylvania_situation_report.md).

**Shared edition.** The following reading also discusses [p129 A7](129.md#source-p129-a7), [p129 A8](129.md#source-p129-a8), [p137 A4](137.md#source-p137-a4), [p137 A5](137.md#source-p137-a5).

<a id="edition-cases-military-transylvania-situation-report-surviving-transylvania-situation-report"></a>



Prepared by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**.

This is a proposed cross-page assembly of an eight-part message marked 1840 / 18.40, 8 TLE, LP v NKJ. Parts 1, 7 and 8 survive on pp128–129; p137 supplies part 4 and conditional partial readings of interference-damaged parts 5 and 6. Parts 2 and 3 remain unlocated. All uses of the Nov4–6 key retain its published square and ranks.

The headings conflict: pp128–129 say 5 November with different evening receipt times; p137 has a 6 November page heading and 08.14 on 5 November in its receipt line, alongside the 18.40 origin. Matching headers, part numbers and content support the association but do not resolve those dates or prove an exact transmission history.

<a id="edition-cases-military-transylvania-situation-report-missing-and-unread-material"></a>

### Missing and unread material

The p128 copy explicitly states that parts 2–6 are missing. The separate p137 page supplies independent surviving material for 4–6. It does not restore parts 2/3, and part 6 has no stated length. A [separate conditional A6 edition](../military/p137_publicity_fragment.md) proposes 25 letters in a 254-slot frame, preserving 102 unknown positions and the equally compatible 256/258-slot alternatives. Its polarity and intervening verb remain unread.

<a id="edition-cases-military-transylvania-situation-report-p137-a5"></a>

### p137 A5

The conditional complete reading orders the removal of economic and
administrative staffs before military movements begin:

**Readable German — conditional complete part-5 proposal:**

> Anschliessend muessen vor Beginn militaerischer Bewegungen Personal der
> Wirtschafts- und Verwaltungsstaebe ab 6. November abgeschoben werden.

The proposal reaches **126/126 positions**, including two separately priced
`X` separators after `WIRTSCHAFTS` and `WERDEN`. Each separator supplies one
missing coordinate while retaining its observed half. The full part costs
**seven observed substitutions, four printed-mask fills and 37 missing-coordinate
fills** under the earlier conditional 0/37 interference frame. The source-68
V alternative lowers the substitution total to six. The literal `MUESSEN`
and date label `6` are retained.

The [completion account](../../experiments/p137_governing_clause/README.md#completing-the-two-separators)
shows all 36 possible residual label pairs before the punctuation choice.
This completes the proposed reading of part 5; the missing parts and the
separate part-6 fragment remain as described above.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — conditional 0/37 interference-loss allocation, selected by the stated prefix crib:**

```text
ANS?HLI?SSE?DMUE?SEN?ORB?GNN?MI?I?AER?SC??RSO?RG?N?ENP?RS??ALD?RW?R?SSH?FT??UNQ?ER?K?TUN?SS??EBE?B6?N?VEM?ER??GES?HO?E?WER?EN?
```

**Edited output — same conditional interference-loss model; four partial word completions:**

```text
ANSCHLIESSENDMUESSEN?ORB?GNN?MILITAERISCHERSO?RG?N?ENPERSONALDERW?R?SSH?FT??UNQ?ER?K?TUN?SS??EBE?B6?NOVEMBERABGESCHOBENWERDEN?
```

</details>

Printed 215 / advertised 252 means 37 missing coordinates in addition to four printed dashes. All 38 allocations between the two explicit INTERFERENCE locations are retained. The 0/37 model is the unique zero-observed-error fit for the explicit 20-character prefix ANSCHLIESSENDMUESSEN; this remains conditional on that crib. Four compatible word spans fill 21 erased coordinates without changing any observed coordinate. Twenty plaintext positions and the awkward observed middle wording remain unresolved. This is a partial reading, not a completed sentence.

A [separate staff-vocabulary proposal](../../experiments/p137_optional_staff_vocabulary/README.md)
reads `WIRTSCHAFTS?UNDVERWALTUNGSSTAEBE` under the same conditional 0/37 frame.
It adds three observed-coordinate substitutions and ten missing-coordinate
fills; the alternative reading of one overtyped source glyph is retained
separately. Ten plaintext positions remain unresolved, including the literal
`?B6?` field. The primary partial edition above and its zero-substitution
price remain unchanged. Independent witnesses attest the two staff compounds,
not this complete clause or its historical execution.

The [governing-clause supplement](../../experiments/p137_governing_clause/README.md)
first extends the optional reading to **124/126 positions**: `VORBEGINN
MILITAERISCHER BEWEGUNGEN` and `AB6XNOVEMBER`. Relative to the staff layer,
it adds four observed substitutions, one printed-mask fill and seven
missing-coordinate fills. The separate `AB6X` proposal needs only two fills
and preserves the observed 6. The two final separator fills give the complete
optional reading displayed above; the governing clause remains a contextual
reconstruction.

<a id="edition-cases-military-transylvania-situation-report-evidence-and-totals"></a>

### Evidence and totals

The five readable physical sources provide 550 modeled plaintext positions: 499 fixed under their declared raw geometries and 530 after the stated candidates. Costs are six observed-coordinate substitutions, seven fills of printed dashes/invalid glyphs, and 24 missing-coordinate fills. The 74-slot part 6 now has its own [25-letter conditional catalogue entry](../military/p137_publicity_fragment.md); it remains excluded from these five-source totals. That separate model has zero raw fixed positions and does not establish the missing sentence.

The earlier corpus screen already recognized parts 1/7/8. Lasry et al. describe a different thirteen-part report of 3 November in their Table 3; this edition makes no first historical decipherment claim. A complete 788-block exact-window search found only one short 12-coordinate incidental lead and no missing part 2/3.
